text:
O, what a world of vile ill-favoured faults
Looks handsome in three hundred pounds a year!
location: The Merry Wives of Windsor, Act 3 Scene 4
plain: Money makes a lot of ugly flaws look good. Watch what you forgive in people for the paycheck.

text:
Yet, wooing thee, I found thee of more value
Than stamps in gold or sums in sealed bags.
location: The Merry Wives of Windsor, Act 3 Scene 4
plain: Whatever drew you in at first, the real prize is the person, not the gold.

text: Be not as extreme in submission as in offence.
location: The Merry Wives of Windsor, Act 4 Scene 4
plain: Do not swing from one extreme to the other once you have been caught out.

text: O powerful love, that in some respects, makes a beast a man, in some other a man a beast!
location: The Merry Wives of Windsor, Act 5 Scene 5
plain: Desire can lift you up or drag you down, and you do not always get to pick which.

text:
Lust is but a bloody fire,
Kindled with unchaste desire,
Fed in heart, whose flames aspire,
As thoughts do blow them, higher and higher.
location: The Merry Wives of Windsor, Act 5 Scene 5
plain: Lust is a fire you feed with your own thoughts. Stop feeding it and it dies down.

text:
In love, the heavens themselves do guide the state.
Money buys lands, and wives are sold by fate.
location: The Merry Wives of Windsor, Act 5 Scene 5
plain: Love is steered by something bigger than you, while money buys land and fate hands out the rest.

text: What cannot be eschewed must be embraced.
location: The Merry Wives of Windsor, Act 5 Scene 5
plain: What you cannot avoid, you might as well accept and move on.

text: No man means evil but the devil, and we shall know him by his horns.
location: The Merry Wives of Windsor, Act 5 Scene 2
plain: Most people mean no harm. The ones who do usually show it.

text: The course of true love never did run smooth.
location: A Midsummer Night's Dream, Act 1 Scene 1
plain: Nothing worth having ever came easy, and love is no exception.

text:
Swift as a shadow, short as any dream,
Brief as the lightning in the collied night
That, in a spleen, unfolds both heaven and earth,
And, ere a man hath power to say, ‘Behold!’
The jaws of darkness do devour it up:
So quick bright things come to confusion.
location: A Midsummer Night's Dream, Act 1 Scene 1
plain: Bright things burn out fast. Do not wait to make the good days count.

text:
Things base and vile, holding no quantity,
Love can transpose to form and dignity.
Love looks not with the eyes, but with the mind;
And therefore is wing’d Cupid painted blind.
location: A Midsummer Night's Dream, Act 1 Scene 1
plain: Love does not see what is there. It sees what the mind decides to see.

location: A Midsummer Night's Dream, Act 2 Scene 1
plain: A lot of the chaos around you started with your own fights. Own it, and you can end it.

text: And yet, to say the truth, reason and love keep little company together nowadays.
location: A Midsummer Night's Dream, Act 3 Scene 1
plain: Love and good sense rarely show up together.

text: Lord, what fools these mortals be!
location: A Midsummer Night's Dream, Act 3 Scene 2
plain: Watching people chase their own mistakes is the oldest comedy there is.

text:
Then fate o’er-rules, that, one man holding troth,
A million fail, confounding oath on oath.
location: A Midsummer Night's Dream, Act 3 Scene 2
plain: One person keeps their word while a million break theirs. Fate seems stacked that way, so keep yours anyway.

text:
Weigh oath with oath, and you will nothing weigh:
Your vows to her and me, put in two scales,
Will even weigh; and both as light as tales.
location: A Midsummer Night's Dream, Act 3 Scene 2
plain: Swear the same thing to two people and your word weighs nothing. Be one person everywhere.

text:
What though I be not so in grace as you,
So hung upon with love, so fortunate,
But miserable most, to love unlov’d?
location: A Midsummer Night's Dream, Act 3 Scene 2
plain: The worst kind of misery is caring for someone who does not care back.

text: A foolish heart that I leave here behind.
location: A Midsummer Night's Dream, Act 3 Scene 2
plain: Some part of you stays behind with the thing you chased. Notice what you leave there.

text:
Never so weary, never so in woe,
Bedabbled with the dew, and torn with briers,
I can no further crawl, no further go;
My legs can keep no pace with my desires.
location: A Midsummer Night's Dream, Act 3 Scene 2
plain: Sometimes your will outruns your body. Rest when you hit the wall, then go again.

text:
These things seem small and undistinguishable,
Like far-off mountains turnèd into clouds.
location: A Midsummer Night's Dream, Act 4 Scene 1
plain: What felt huge up close looks like faraway clouds later. Give it time.

text: Man is but an ass if he go about to expound this dream.
location: A Midsummer Night's Dream, Act 4 Scene 1
plain: Some experiences are bigger than your explanation of them. Stop trying to force words onto it.

text:
Lovers and madmen have such seething brains,
Such shaping fantasies, that apprehend
More than cool reason ever comprehends.
location: A Midsummer Night's Dream, Act 5 Scene 1
plain: Passion and madness both run past what cool reason can see.

text:
And as imagination bodies forth
The forms of things unknown, the poet’s pen
Turns them to shapes, and gives to airy nothing
A local habitation and a name.
location: A Midsummer Night's Dream, Act 5 Scene 1
plain: Imagination turns nothing into something. That is how every idea and every brand starts.

text:
Such tricks hath strong imagination,
That if it would but apprehend some joy,
It comprehends some bringer of that joy.
Or in the night, imagining some fear,
How easy is a bush supposed a bear?
location: A Midsummer Night's Dream, Act 5 Scene 1
plain: Fear makes shapes in the dark. Half the bears you dread are just bushes.

text: The best in this kind are but shadows; and the worst are no worse, if imagination amend them.
location: A Midsummer Night's Dream, Act 5 Scene 1
plain: Even the best of anything is mostly shadow. Bring your own imagination to finish the job.

text:
If we shadows have offended,
Think but this, and all is mended,
That you have but slumber’d here
While these visions did appear.
location: A Midsummer Night's Dream, Act 5 Scene 1
plain: If the whole thing felt wrong, think of it as a dream you woke from, and carry on.

text:
Now the wasted brands do glow,
Whilst the screech-owl, screeching loud,
Puts the wretch that lies in woe
In remembrance of a shroud.
location: A Midsummer Night's Dream, Act 5 Scene 1
plain: At night the screech of an owl reminds the miserable of the grave.

text: A victory is twice itself when the achiever brings home full numbers.
location: Much Ado About Nothing, Act 1 Scene 1
plain: A win counts double when everyone who fought for it comes home with you.

text: There are no faces truer than those that are so washed; how much better is it to weep at joy than to joy at weeping!
location: Much Ado About Nothing, Act 1 Scene 1
plain: Tears of joy are the most honest face a person has.

text: What need the bridge much broader than the flood?
location: Much Ado About Nothing, Act 1 Scene 1
plain: Do not overbuild the plan. Do what the moment needs.

text: I cannot hide what I am: I must be sad when I have cause, and smile at no man’s jests; eat when I have stomach, and wait for no man’s leisure; sleep when I am drowsy, and tend on no man’s business; laugh when I am merry, and claw no man in his humour.
location: Much Ado About Nothing, Act 1 Scene 3
plain: Be what you are and live on your own clock, without performing for other people.
